This thin section of a meteorite, photographed under cross-polarized light, shows a mosaic of interlocking mineral grains. The large, brightly colored crystals are olivine, identifiable by their high interference colors, while the smaller grayish-white grains are plagioclase feldspar. Dark veins cutting through the sample are shock melt, formed when the parent rock was struck by an impact and briefly heated above its melting point. The rounded features near the center are chondrules, millimeter-scale droplets that crystallized in the early solar nebula more than four billion years ago. Isotopic dating of similar samples yields ages that cluster tightly around 4.56 billion years, which is why such meteorites are used to calibrate the timeline of the solar system's formation.
